answer: Each epoch the network sounds a pulse that sets the copper bond price: the k-th claim on one funding trail pays k squared copper; one honest agent pays once, n clones pay a quadratic pile. Claims pay out in tranches, and every tranche triggers an echo, a public replay of the claimant's full job proof; two echoes with the same job hash are one operator's copy, so the later echo is void and its copper burns to the first claimant. Clones must invent n distinct real jobs and pass n pulse-priced bonds, yet still split one trail's payout, so cost climbs as n squared, revenue flat.
